title: Binning and coverage spec — Dedicated GPU tiling
summary: Worked example and spec for assigning reserved dedicated GPU capacity per contract using fractile binning and coverage-hours. Introduces alpha headroom factor, per-region coverage goals, and a compact allocation matrix for operations.
body:
Sheet: Binning & Coverage — Dedicated GPU Allocations (worked example)

Columns: Contract, Customer, Region, GPU Type, Entitlement (reserved GPUs), Baseline 50th FR, 90th FR, Coverage Target (% hours), Coverage Hours/week, Burstable Pool (GPUs), Alpha headroom, Final Reserved (GPUs), Notes

Rows:
C-331: AcmePayments, us-west1, A100-80GB, 24, 18, 30, 95, 1596, 4, 1.10, 26, "high-throughput RL inference; allow burst for monthly spikes"
C-419: GenEdu, eu-west1, H100-80GB, 8, 6, 11, 90, 1512, 1, 1.18, 9, "steady classroom workloads with predictable diurnal; burst 1"
C-502: HealthScale, us-east1, A100-40GB, 16, 12, 20, 97, 1658, 3, 1.12, 18, "HIPAA customer; keep regional redundancy for failover"
C-620: RetailMax, ap-southeast1, A100-80GB, 12, 9, 16, 92, 1540, 2, 1.15, 13, "seasonal e-commerce; plan runway for Nov/Dec"

Methodology notes:
- We bucket per-contract request-rate samples into quantiles (50th and 90th used here) over a rolling 90-day window.
- Coverage Hours/week = target% * total hours/week (168) -> used to convert a percent SLO into reserved-hours footprint.
- Alpha headroom = multiplicative fudge to account for cold-starts, lost capacity, and kernel-level variance. Alpha is selected by risk tier: critical=1.12; standard=1.15; flexible=1.10.
- Final Reserved (GPUs) = ceil( Entitlement * max( (90th_FR / Entitlement), alpha ) ) but we clamp to contract cap if present. (Worked examples above follow this rule and include burstable pool.)

Operational heuristics:
- Burstable Pool: small dedicated buffer per-region (1–4 GPUs) carved from local unreserved capacity to cover transient overshoot. Replenished by nightly rebalancing.
- Cross-region fallback: If region-level reserved >90% utilization for 6+ hours, routing policy should failover to compatible variants in adjacent region (subject to data locality rules).
- Recompute quantiles weekly; if 90th_FR grows >15% week-over-week for two consecutive weeks, trigger capacity onboarding ticket (JIRA-INFRA-ONBOARD).

Allocation matrix snippet (for SRE/Capacity UI ingestion):
- contract_id: C-331 | region: us-west1 | gpu_type: A100-80GB | reserved_gpus: 26 | burstable: 4 | coverage_pct: 95 | alpha: 1.10 | notes: high-throughput
- contract_id: C-419 | region: eu-west1 | gpu_type: H100-80GB | reserved_gpus: 9 | burstable: 1 | coverage_pct: 90 | alpha: 1.18 | notes: classroom load
- contract_id: C-502 | region: us-east1 | gpu_type: A100-40GB | reserved_gpus: 18 | burstable: 3 | coverage_pct: 97 | alpha: 1.12 | notes: compliance

Risk considerations:
- Over-reserving reduces shared pool efficiency; under-reserving increases throttles/failures that impact SLA. This spec biases slightly to the conservative side for "critical" customers.
- Alpha should be reviewed after each major runtime/kernel change; quantile estimates become stale when model sizes or sequence length distributions shift.

Open questions for review:
- Should we use 95th FR instead of 90th for top-tier contracts? Pros/cons outlined in the attached simulation results (linked artifact).
- How to reconcile burstable pool billing with customer invoices (currently on ops to reconcile monthly).

Next steps:
- Run 14-day experiment with alpha adjustments: {critical:1.08->1.12, standard:1.12->1.15} and collect missed-coverage events.
- Add an automated alert to capacity dashboard for "90th_FR growth > 15% x 2 weeks" (Confluence playbook linked).
- Finalize contract cap enforcement behavior (soft cap vs hard cap) with commercial team.

Appendix: Quick formulas (for ops):
- coverage_hours_week = round( coverage_pct/100 * 168 )
- final_reserved = ceil( max( entitlement, ceil(90th_FR * alpha) ) )
- burst_replenish_window = 04:00-06:00 UTC daily

This doc is intentionally concise; for the full simulation matrices and python notebooks see linked_artifacts above.
